In [[algebraic geometry]], '''Behrend's trace formula''' is a generalization of the [[Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula]] to a [[smooth stack|smooth]] [[algebraic stack]] over a [[finite field]] conjectured in 1993 <ref>Behrend, K. [http://www.math.ubc.ca/~behrend/thesis.pdf The Lefschetz Trace Formula for the Moduli Stack of Principal Bundles.] PhD dissertation.</ref> and proven in 2003 <ref>{{citation|last=Behrend|first= Kai|author-link=Kai Behrend|url= http://www.math.ubc.ca/~behrend/ladic.pdf|title= Derived l-adic categories for algebraic stacks|journal= [[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume= 163|year= 2003|doi= 10.1090/memo/0774}}</ref> by [[Kai Behrend]]. Unlike the classical one, the formula counts points in the "[[stack (mathematics)|stacky way]]"; it takes into account the presence of nontrivial automorphisms.

The desire for the formula comes from the fact that it applies to the [[moduli stack of principal bundles]] on a curve over a finite field (in some instances indirectly, via the [[Harder–Narasimhan stratification]], as the moduli stack is not of finite type.<ref>K. Behrend, A. Dhillon, [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503383 Connected components of moduli stacks of torsors via Tamagawa numbers]</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Cohomological Formulation (Lecture 3)|url=https://www.math.ias.edu/~lurie/282ynotes/LectureIII-Cohomology.pdf|publisher=Institute for Advanced Study|first=Jacob|last=Lurie|author-link=Jacob Lurie|work= Tamagawa Numbers via Nonabelian Poincare Duality (282y)|date=Spring 2014}}</ref>) See the [[moduli stack of principal bundles]] and references therein for the precise formulation in this case.

[[Pierre Deligne]] found an example<!-- which we should include here as well--><ref>{{harvnb|Behrend|2003|loc=Proposition 6.4.11}}</ref> that shows the formula may be interpreted as a sort of the [[Selberg trace formula]].

A proof of the formula in the context of the [[six operations]] formalism developed by [[Yves Laszlo]] and Martin Olsson<ref>*{{cite arXiv |first1=Yves |last1=Laszlo |first2=Martin |last2=Olsson |eprint=math/0512097v2 |title=The six operations for sheaves on Artin stacks I: Finite Coefficients |year=2006  }}</ref> is given by Shenghao Sun.<ref>{{harvnb|Shenghao|2011}}</ref>

== Formulation ==
By definition, if ''C'' is a category in which each object has finitely many automorphisms, the number of points in <math>C</math> is denoted by
:<math>\# C = \sum_p  {1 \over \# \operatorname{Aut}(p)},</math>
with the sum running over representatives ''p'' of all isomorphism classes in ''C''. (The series may diverge in general.) The formula states: for a smooth algebraic stack ''X'' of finite type over a finite field <math>\mathbb{F}_q</math> and the [[arithmetic Frobenius|"arithmetic" Frobenius]] <math>\phi^{-1}: X \to X</math>, i.e., the inverse of the usual geometric Frobenius <math>\phi</math> in Grothendieck's formula,<ref>To define Frobenius <math>\phi</math> on a stack ''X'', let <math>\phi: \overline{\mathbb{F}_q} \to \overline{\mathbb{F}_q}, x \mapsto x^q</math>. Then we have <math>id \times \phi: X \times_{\mathbb{F}_q} \overline{\mathbb{F}_q} \to X \times_{\mathbb{F}_q} \overline{\mathbb{F}_q}</math>, which is the Frobenius on ''X'', also denoted by <math>\phi</math>.</ref><ref>{{harvnb|Behrend|2003|loc=Corollary 6.4.10}}</ref>
:<math>\# X (\mathbb{F}_q) = q^{\dim X} \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} (-1)^i \operatorname{tr} \left (\phi^{-1}; H^i(X, \Q_l) \right ).</math>

Here, it is crucial that the [[cohomology of a stack]] is with respect to the [[smooth topology]] (not etale).

When ''X'' is a variety, the smooth cohomology is the same as etale one and, via the [[Poincaré duality]], this is equivalent to Grothendieck's trace formula. (But the proof of Behrend's trace formula relies on Grothendieck's formula, so this does not subsume Grothendieck's.)

== Simple example ==
Consider <math>B\mathbb{G}_m = [\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{F}_q/\mathbb{G}_m]</math>, the [[classifying stack]] of the multiplicative [[group scheme]] (that is, <math>\mathbb{G}_m(R) = R^\times</math>). By definition, <math>B \mathbb{G}_m(\mathbb{F}_q)</math> is the category of [[torsor|principal]] <math>\mathbb{G}_m</math>-bundles over <math>\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{F}_q</math>, which has only one isomorphism class (since all such bundles are trivial by [[Lang's theorem]]). Its group of automorphisms is <math>\mathbb{G}_m</math>, which means that the number of <math>\mathbb{F}_q</math>-isomorphisms is <math>\#\mathbb{G}_m(\mathbb{F}_q) = \#\mathbb{F}_q^\times = q-1</math>.

On the other hand, we may compute the ''l''-adic cohomology of <math>B\mathbb{G}_m</math> directly. We remark that in the topological setting, we have <math>B\C^\times \cong \mathbb{CP}^\infty</math> (where <math>B\C^\times</math> now denotes the usual classifying space of a [[topological group]]), whose rational cohomology ring is a [[polynomial ring]] in one generator ([[Borel's theorem]]), but we shall not use this directly. If we wish to stay in the world of algebraic geometry, we may instead "approximate" <math>B\mathbb{G}_m</math> by projective spaces of larger and larger dimension. Thus  we consider the map <math>B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathbb{P}^N</math> induced by the <math>\mathbb{G}_m</math>-bundle corresponding to <math>\mathcal{O}(1).</math> This map induces an isomorphism in cohomology in degrees up to ''2N''. Thus the even (resp. odd) Betti numbers of <math>B \mathbb{G}_m</math> are 1 (resp. 0), and the ''l''-adic Galois representation on the ''(2n)''th cohomology group is the ''n''th power of the cyclotomic character. The second part is a consequence of the fact that the cohomology of <math>\mathbb{P}^N</math> is generated by algebraic cycle classes. This shows that

:<math>\sum_{i \ge 0} (-1)^i \operatorname{tr} \left (\phi^{-1}; H^i(B\mathbb{G}_m, \Q_l) \right ) =  1 + \frac{1}{q} + \frac{1}{q^2} + \cdots = \frac{q}{q-1}.</math>

Note that

:<math>\dim B \mathbb{G}_m = \dim \operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{F}_q - \dim \mathbb{G}_m = -1.</math>

Multiplying by <math>q^{-1}</math>, one obtains the predicted equality.
